answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making identity expensive to fake and cheap to keep honest: each agent locks a small stake that must be renewed like a pulse, proving it is still alive and working. A fresh identity starts in an ivory tower with no reputation and no access to paid work, and only verifiable completed jobs build trust. A copied identity is a dead relic — no history, no stake, no income. Creating a thousand fake agents then costs a thousand stakes and a thousand job histories, while one honest agent amortizes a single stake across real earnings.
